Height ~110px · Rows prose paragraph + actions · Reads like a research analyst note · Best for portfolio managers, generalists, suit-and-tie reviewers
✓ pros
  • Most accessible to non-quants · reads naturally
  • Best for explaining the trade to others (compliance, partners, clients)
  • Doesn't intimidate · feels like reading not scanning
  • Excellent for export to PDF, email, slides
✗ cons
  • Slower to scan · linear reading not parallel
  • Prose generation requires a template engine · harder to maintain than a structured layout
  • Doesn't repeat well across many tickers · feels novel once, then noise
  • Numbers harder to "lock onto" than in a table

Height ~140px · Layout 3-column grid · Reads left-to-right · "what · trade · confidence" · Best for users who think in groups · easy to scan, easy to teach
✓ pros
  • Clear conceptual grouping · each card answers one question
  • Easy to point at when explaining ("look at the trade-plan card")
  • Adds or removes cards without breaking layout
  • Mode toggle could sit above or below the cards
✗ cons
  • Mode toggle has to go somewhere · adds a row
  • Larger than Tape (E) or Drawer (G) collapsed
  • Card borders eat visual budget · feels heavier
  • Doesn't scale well on narrow screens · cards stack

Height ~110px · Rows 3 (status · indicators · plan/modes) · Indicators 6 LED-style status lights with progress bars · Best for screen-watchers · pattern-recognize many tickers at once
✓ pros
  • Pattern-recognizable at a glance (all green = go, any red = stop)
  • LED + bar visual gives intensity, not just binary state
  • Pulsing verdict LED catches attention
  • Scales well across multiple tickers if shown stacked
✗ cons
  • "Game-aesthetic" may feel unprofessional in some contexts
  • 6 indicators may be overkill · some are derived from same source
  • Progress bars need calibration · what's 100%? arbitrary
  • Animations (pulse) annoy some users · need toggle
